messages:
julia (support): heads up — GlobalFin reported a sharp p99 increase for Venicex-2.1 after onboarding at 10:12 UTC. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (long-context >12k). Customer sees 504s and higher token billing.
linh (oncall): on it. any repro payload from them?
julia (support): pasted sample in ticket: long legal doc (~14k tokens). They say it started immediately after we flipped their routing to venicex-2.1.
adeel (eng-runtime): pulling logs for that tenant. I see a pattern: tokenizer falling back to slowpath for long inputs and we’re also seeing KV cache invalidations around sequence boundary. snippets:
```
[2026-03-17T10:15:42Z] tenant=gf corp request_id=abc123 tokenizer=venicex-2.1 path=slow_path reason="merge_overflow" time_ms=512
[2026-03-17T10:15:42Z] tenant=gf corp kvcache=invalidated reason="pad_align" seq_len=14120
[2026-03-17T10:15:42Z] runtime=serve node=rdw-rt-14 latency_ms=1248 p99 spike
```
sophia (ml): that tokenizer change in 2.1 adjusted BPE merging to improve avg tokens, but it added an expensive normalization for multi-byte sequences near long boundaries — will cause CPU stalls and kvcache churn.
julia (support): customer is pretty upset — asks for mitigation now. can we give them a quick fallback?
adeel (eng-runtime): yes. two immediate mitigations we can do: 1) route their traffic back to venicex-2.0 (compat tokenizer) for the next 24h; 2) enable long-sequence prefix caching bypass to avoid kvcache invalidation spikes for sequences >10k. Both low-risk.
linh (oncall): i can run the routing change as a canary for that tenant. need the tenant id and confirmation to proceed.
julia (support): tenant id GF-9876. customer approved fallback to venicex-2.0 and wants status updates every 30m.
adeel (eng-runtime): plan:
- step A: update routing policy for GF-9876 -> venicex-2.0 (canary)
- step B: enable kvcache bypass flag for GF-9876 long_seq=true
- step C: monitor p95/p99 and errors for 30m, rollback if any regressions
Commands:
```bash
# routing update (control plane)
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing/update -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"tenant":"GF-9876","target":"venicex-2.0","mode":"canary","weight":100}'
# enable kvcache bypass (feature flag)
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/flags -d '{"tenant":"GF-9876","flag":"kvcache_long_seq_bypass","value":true}'
```
linh (oncall): running step A now. starting canary rollout to 3% -> 20% -> 100% (expected ~8m). will post updates. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
deploy-bot: deploy/route-update started by linh — change_id=route-GF-4365
adeel (eng-runtime): while canary is rolling, small optimization: increase local tokenizer timeout from 250ms -> 800ms for venicex-2.1 so requests don't fail while they route. This reduces churn but may increase tail latency briefly — acceptable interim.
sophia (ml): also queueing a quick rollback for tokenizer patch: revert the normalization for >8k sequences in 2.1 branch, but that takes ~2-3h testing. prefer routing fallback first.
julia (support): i've told GlobalFin we will route them back and apply flags; offering 2 days of credits for disruption. they appreciated quick response.
linh (oncall): canary metrics update: p99 for GF-9876 dropped from 3.2s -> 720ms after moving to venicex-2.0; error rate (504) down to 0.2% from 2.8%. holding for 30m. :white_check_mark:
adeel (eng-runtime): flag applied for kvcache bypass. monitoring aggregated logs for "kvcache=invalidated" — incidence down 87%.
ops-bot: metric alert suppressed for GF-9876 p99 on venicex-2.1 by linh until 2026-03-17T13:00:00Z (manual suppression).
sophia (ml): filed a follow-up ticket for tokenizer revert PR: PR#4573, reviewers @sophia @adeel. will include regression tests with 12k-16k sequences.
julia (support): customer updated: "Thanks — perf looks back to normal on our side. Please keep us posted."
linh (oncall): will keep the routing pinned to venicex-2.0 for 24h, then coordinate a staged re-onboard with ml+runtime after the tokenizer revert. closing loop with customer after full verification.
adeel (eng-runtime): postmortem notes to add: - cause: venicex-2.1 tokenizer normalization edge for long multi-byte sequences; - impact: p99 surge and kvcache invalidation for long-context tenants; - mitigation: tenant-level routing fallback, kvcache bypass flag, temp timeout increase; - long-term: revert normalization change and add longseq unit/regression tests.
julia (support): thanks all — updating ticket and setting status -> remediation in progress. will post final once PR merged and we re-onboard. :v:
